scope: read-only binary, launch, layout, and timing audit

fixup.synchronization: standalone launch after main; no BAR, ATOM, or MEMBAR in fixup

address_mapping.warp_destination_address_shape: 32 distinct rows for a single store issue

runtime_loader_allocation_report.note: loader allocation floors; cuobjdump reports zero static shared/local/stack

fixup.synchronization: standalone launch after main; source null-ids path has no barrier; normalized SASS has no BAR, ATOM, or MEMBAR

address_mapping.destination_index: j*512 + i within the selected tile

fold_and_traffic.fold_order: nonfinal contributors in descending owner order, then final contributor
fold_and_traffic.candidate_execution: zero plus all scratch contributors in frozen descriptor order
fold_and_traffic.llama_execution: final contribution already in destination; predecessor scratch is visited by descending owner and then added to destination
fold_and_traffic.note: logical payload excludes cache-line and sector amplification; candidate destination address dispersion is therefore materially more important than the 0.5 MiB payload delta

low_register_control.caveat: historical all-partials map order differs from the frozen descending-predecessor order; launch, payload, and destination mapping are equivalent

launch_floor.label: proven
launch_floor.basis: both routes use one standalone post-main launch and llama completes nontrivial fixup work in 8.640 us

logical_traffic_volume.label: proven_for_payload_inferred_for_hardware_cost
logical_traffic_volume.basis: fixup payload differs by only 0.5 MiB and full main-plus-fixup route payload differs by only 0.5 MiB

fold_order.label: proven_contract
fold_order.basis: both visit nonfinal owners in descending order and place the final contribution last; direct-final generated controls were bit exact but slower

compiler_spill.label: strong_inference
compiler_spill.basis: 30-register zero-stack historical control with equivalent launch/payload/address mapping remains at 25.088 us versus current 25.056 us

scalar_address_control.label: inference
scalar_address_control.basis: llama has substantially more static integer/control work yet is faster; descriptor payload is small

destination_coalescing.label: proven_address_shape_inferred_timing_dominance
destination_coalescing.basis: candidate warp stores touch 32 locations 16 KiB apart while llama warp stores one contiguous 128-byte span

grid_parallelism.label: proven_structure_inferred_timing_dominance
grid_parallelism.basis: candidate exposes 1024 active warps in 128 blocks, llama exposes 2048 active warps in 512 active blocks on the 170-SM target

classification.overall: 25.056 us is not a launch-floor, fold-order, raw-byte-volume, or spill result. It is most consistent with destination transaction amplification plus insufficient grid granularity; their individual shares are not yet causally separated.
